Khi nói, người bản xứ gần như luôn rút g: In speech, native speakers almost always use short forms: I'm, you're, he's, it's. The one exception is a positive short answer: "Yes, I am" (never "Yes, I'm").

My sister là một người (ngôi thứ ba số í: "My sister" is one person (third person singular) → is. Am goes only with I; are goes with you, we, they and plural nouns; be is the base form and never comes straight after a subject.
We đi với are. is dành cho he, she, it v: "We" takes are. Is is for he, she, it and singular nouns; am is only for I; be is the base form, so it doesn't fit here.
I đi với am → I am hungry. is và are khô: "I" takes am → I am hungry. Is and are never go with I, and in English you "are hungry" – you don't "have hunger".
Your parents là số nhiều → Are đứng đầu: "Your parents" is plural → Are goes at the start of the question. Is is for singular subjects, Am is only for I, and Do never combines with be – to make a question with be, just move be to the front.
Tom là một người → is not = isn't. aren': "Tom" is one person → is not = isn't. Aren't is for plurals; not on its own leaves the sentence without a verb; don't is never used with be.
Trả lời ngắn khẳng định không rút gọn →: A positive short answer is never contracted → Yes, I am. The short form 'm can't end a sentence, and are and is don't go with I.
Câu hỏi dùng is → trả lời phủ định No, i: The question uses is → the negative answer is "No, it isn't." Aren't is for plurals, not alone has no verb, and doesn't is only for questions with does.
Nói tuổi: be + số + years old → She is 2: Age: be + number + years old → She is 25 years old. Has is the wrong verb, the third sentence is missing be, and are doesn't go with she.
Phủ định với be: S + is + not → My phone: Negative with be: S + is + not → My phone is not on the desk. Not must come after is; does not doesn't go with be; are doesn't fit "my phone" (singular).
Câu hỏi với be: từ để hỏi + be + chủ ngữ: Questions with be: question word + be + subject → Where are your keys? "Keys" is plural, so it's are, not is; the other two sentences have the wrong word order or no be.

My brother and I = we (số nhiều) → phải: "My brother and I" = we (plural) → it must be are, so (C) is wrong. "My brother", "and I" and "at the cinema" are all correct.

"My best friend" is one person → is.

The subject I always takes am.

"Children" is the plural of child → are.

Phủ định với we: are not, rút gọn aren't: Negative with we: are not, short form aren't.

Negative: add not right after are.

Hai người làm chủ ngữ → số nhiều → are +: Two people as the subject → plural → are + the plural noun farmers.
Nối hai câu bằng and; lần nhắc thứ hai t: Join the two sentences with and; the second time, replace Lan with she so it sounds natural.

↓ Không có trợ động từ? Mượn do / does /: ↓ No auxiliary? Borrow do / does / did
Đuôi luôn dùng ĐẠI TỪ: this/that → it, t: Tags always use a PRONOUN: this/that → it, these/those → they, nobody → they
Xác nhận điều mình gần như chắc chắn (gi: Checking something you're almost sure of (falling tone)

Trả lời ngắn tránh lặp lại cả câu: Short answers save you repeating the whole sentence
Trả lời câu hỏi đuôi phủ định theo SỰ TH: Answer a negative question tag according to the FACTS, not according to whether the speaker is "right". You don't smoke, do you? – No, I don't (= that's right, I don't smoke). Saying "Yes" means you DO smoke.
Trong giao tiếp thân mật có thể nói Me t: In casual conversation you can say "Me too" / "Me neither" instead of "So do I" / "Neither do I".
Đuôi phải lặp lại trợ động từ và đại từ: The tag must repeat the auxiliary and the pronoun from the main clause – don't use "isn't it" for everything.
To agree with a negative statement, use Neither.
Câu chính dùng động từ thường ở quá khứ: The main clause has an ordinary verb in the past → the tag is didn't.
Trong Speaking, không cần dùng câu hỏi đ: In Speaking you don't need question tags with the examiner, but a short answer plus more detail ("Yes, I do – actually, I…") is a natural way to start. In Listening Section 1, tags are often used to confirm details – watch out for answers that get corrected.
Câu chính khẳng định với have (have book: A positive main clause with have (have booked) → negative tag with the same auxiliary: haven't you? Didn't/don't use the wrong auxiliary; "have you" doesn't switch to negative.
Nobody mang nghĩa phủ định → đuôi khẳng: Nobody is negative in meaning → positive tag with they. "didn't they" is wrong because nobody is already negative; "did he" has the wrong subject; "noticed they" has the wrong structure.
Ngoại lệ: I am → câu hỏi đuôi là aren't: Exception: I am → the tag is aren't I? We don't say "amn't I" or "am not I"; "isn't it" has the wrong subject.
Câu trước có never (phủ định) → đồng ý d: The first sentence has never (negative) → agree with "neither do" (ordinary verb use). "So do" is for positive statements; "neither don't" is a double negative; "so don't" is wrong.
Câu rủ rê bắt đầu bằng Let's… luôn dùng: A suggestion starting with Let's… always takes the tag shall we? "Will we", "don't we" and "do we" aren't used after Let's.
Đồng ý với câu khẳng định thì quá khứ (p: Agreeing with a positive past statement (passed) → So did I. "So I did" has the wrong word order; Neither is for negative statements; "So was I" uses the wrong auxiliary.
Câu chính phủ định, chủ ngữ there → đuôi: Negative main clause with there as the subject → tag "are there". "Aren't there" doesn't switch to positive; "are they" has the wrong subject; "isn't it" is completely wrong.
Khẳng định với can → câu hỏi đuôi phủ đị: Positive with can → negative tag can't she? "Can she" doesn't switch to negative; doesn't and isn't are the wrong auxiliaries.
hate là động từ thường, câu khẳng định →: "Hate" is an ordinary verb in a positive sentence → So do I. Neither is for negative statements; "So am I" uses the wrong auxiliary; "So I do" has the wrong word order.
Phần nào sai? \"This (A) is your first I: Which part is wrong? "This (A) is your first IELTS test (B), isn't (C) this (D)?"
Câu hỏi đuôi dùng đại từ it thay cho thi: The tag uses the pronoun it instead of this → isn't it?, so (D) is wrong. "This", "is your first IELTS test" and "isn't" are all correct.
Phần nào sai? \"He hardly (A) ever studi: Which part is wrong? "He hardly (A) ever studies (B), doesn't (C) he (D)?"
Hardly mang nghĩa phủ định → đuôi khẳng: Hardly is negative in meaning → positive tag: does he?, so (C) is wrong. "He hardly", "ever studies" and "he" are all correct.
Phần nào sai? \"I haven't (A) seen that: Which part is wrong? "I haven't (A) seen that film. – So (B) have (C) I (D)."
Đồng ý với câu phủ định (haven't) → Neit: Agreeing with a negative statement (haven't) → Neither have I, so (B) So is wrong. "I haven't", "have" and "I" are all correct.
Văn học thuật tránh khẳng định tuyệt đối: Academic writing avoids absolute claims. Use tend to, may well, it appears that, to some extent… to make claims that are precise, objective and hard to refute.
Nói về xu hướng chung, không phải mọi tr: Talking about general trends, not every case
Đưa ra kết luận dè dặt từ dữ liệu: Drawing a cautious conclusion from data
Đừng “hedge” mọi câu: quan điểm chính (t: Don't hedge every sentence: your main position (thesis) needs to be clear. Hedging works best when you talk about causes, effects, predictions and generalisations about groups of people.
Anh-Mỹ dùng likely như trạng từ ngay sau: American English often uses likely as an adverb right after will: Prices will likely rise next year (= will probably rise). British English prefers "will probably" or "are likely to rise". Both are standard, but never write "Prices are likely rise" (to is missing).
Khái quát hóa quá mức (everyone, destroy: Overgeneralising (everyone, destroys) easily strikes the examiner as unconvincing.
tend to + V nguyên mẫu (to ở đây là một: tend to + base verb (here to is part of the infinitive, not a preposition).
Chồng chất quá nhiều từ thận trọng làm c: Piling up hedges makes a sentence weak and wordy. One is enough.
Hedging giúp bài Task 2 nghe học thuật v: Hedging makes a Task 2 essay sound academic and nuanced – it shows a carefully considered position. In Speaking Part 3, "I'd say…" and "It probably depends on…" are natural hedges too.
tend to + V, chủ ngữ Men số nhiều → tend: tend to + verb, and "Men" is plural → tend. "Tending" leaves no main verb; "are tend" is wrong; "tends" is singular.
It appears that + mệnh đề (dường như) →: It appears that + clause (= it seems) → It appears that… Appear is intransitive, so it has no passive ("is appeared" is wrong); "appearing" leaves no main verb; "is appearing" is the wrong tense.
may well + V = rất có thể → may well con: may well + verb = quite possibly → may well continue. Are, tend and likely can't come before "well + base verb" (likely needs "are likely to").
Cụm cố định: to some extent / to a certa: Fixed phrase: to some extent / to a certain extent. Any, an and many don't go with extent in this phrase.
be likely to + V → is likely to fall. \": be likely to + verb → is likely to fall. "Is tend" is wrong (tend is a verb and can't follow is); possible isn't used with "to + verb" like this (you need "It is possible that…"); probably is an adverb.
Bị động khách quan: It is widely believe: Impersonal passive: It is widely believed that… "Believe" is the base form, "believing" is the wrong form, and "belief" is a noun.
Câu nào thận trọng và đúng ngữ pháp nhất: Which sentence is the most cautious and grammatically correct?
Câu B thận trọng hợp lý; A tuyệt đối, C: Sentence B is suitably cautious: A is absolute, C piles up hedges, and D is ungrammatical. A makes an absolute claim (definitely); C stacks three hedges; D has a grammar error (are tend).
Cấu trúc rào đón There appears/seems to: The hedge There appears/seems to be + noun (= it seems there is…) → There appears to be a link. After appear use "to be", not "being"; appear is intransitive, so it has no passive.
seem + to be + tính từ (dường như…) → se: seem + to be + adjective (= appears to be…) → seem to be less willing. "Seem be" is missing to; "are seem" is wrong because seem is already the main verb.
Câu nào cùng nghĩa, nhưng thận trọng hơn: Which sentence has the same meaning but is more cautious? "Online learning is worse than classroom learning."
can be + for some students giới hạn phạm: "Can be" + "for some students" limits the scope of the claim. Always and must are absolute, so they are no more cautious than the original.
Câu nào cùng nghĩa? “Probably, the bridg: Which sentence has the same meaning? "Probably, the bridge will be finished by 2030."
Probably will → be likely to + V (bị độn: Probably will → be likely to + verb (passive: to be finished). "Tends to finish" describes a habit; "appears finishing" and "likely finishing" are the wrong forms.
Câu nào cùng nghĩa? “People say that the: Which sentence has the same meaning? "People say that the town was founded by monks."
Bị động khách quan: S + is said + to hav: Impersonal passive: S + is said + to have been + past participle (for a past event). "Is said founding" is the wrong form; "It says" is active; "The town says" has the wrong subject.
Câu có may và \"further research is need: The sentence has may and "further research is needed" → the conclusion is still tentative, so use the cautious verb suggest. Prove, confirm and guarantee express certainty, which contradicts the second half.
It ___ be argued that social media has i: It ___ be argued that social media has improved political participation. (choose the hedge)
Cụm rào đón quen thuộc trong văn học thu: A common hedge in academic writing: It could be argued that…
Câu nào dùng cách nói rào đón (hedging): Which sentence uses the most appropriate hedging for academic writing?
tend to + suggest làm nhẹ mức khẳng định: "Tend to" + "suggest" softens the claim – just right for academic writing. The other sentences generalise absolutely (all, always, every, It is a fact), so they can look unsupported.
be likely + to V (có khả năng sẽ…) → are: be likely + to + verb (= will probably…) → are likely to rise. Rose, rising and rise can't follow "be likely".
Động từ khuyết thiếu may + V nguyên mẫu: Modal may + base verb → may be (= might be), used to hedge. "May been", "may being" and "may to be" are all the wrong form after may.
according to + nguồn (theo…) → According: according to + source → According to the survey. Accordingly is an adverb (= therefore) and doesn't take to.
\"further studies are needed\" cho thấy: "Further studies are needed" shows the conclusion is still tentative → suggest. "Prove", "confirm absolutely" and "show without doubt" are too certain and contradict the second half.
It ___ be argued that remote work increa: It ___ be argued that remote work increases productivity. (choose the hedge)
It could be argued that… là cách rào đón: "It could be argued that…" is a formal way to hedge when you put forward a view. "Must", "will" and "should always" make the claim too strong – they aren't hedges.
Online learning ___ to be more popular a: Online learning ___ to be more popular among working adults than among teenagers. (choose the hedge)
appear + to V là cách nói dè dặt (có vẻ): appear + to + verb is a cautious way to say "seems". "Is certainly" and "always is" are absolute; "definitely seems" is grammatical, but definitely cancels out the hedge.
There is ___ evidence that the new polic: There is ___ evidence that the new policy has reduced crime. (choose the hedge)
limited evidence (bằng chứng còn hạn chế: "Limited evidence" suits cautious academic writing. "Every evidence" is ungrammatical (evidence is uncountable); "complete/total evidence" is too absolute and sounds unnatural.
Cấu trúc be likely to + V. \"probably/po: The structure is be likely to + verb. Probably, possibly and perhaps are adverbs and don't fit "are … to rise" (you'd say "will probably rise").
This difference ___ partly explained by: This difference ___ partly explained by the age of the participants. (choose the hedge)
may be + V3 kết hợp partly tạo kết luận: "May be" + past participle together with partly makes a tentative conclusion. "Is surely", "must always be" and "is completely" are too certain and contradict partly.
Most researchers ___ that climate change: Most researchers ___ that climate change affects bird migration. (choose the hedge)
tend to agree (có xu hướng đồng ý) – rào: "Tend to agree" is a hedge that fits "Most researchers". "All agree" and "without exception" contradict most; "must agree" has the wrong meaning (obligation).
The data ___ a link between screen time: The data ___ a link between screen time and poor sleep. (choose the hedge)
indicate (cho thấy) là động từ báo cáo d: Indicate is a cautious reporting verb. The other options make absolute claims, which don't suit cautious academic writing.
In ___ cases, the side effects were mild: In ___ cases, the side effects were mild. (choose the hedge)
In most cases giới hạn phạm vi khẳng địn: "In most cases" limits the scope of the claim (hedging with a quantifier). "All of the cases" and "every case" are absolute; "every cases" is also ungrammatical; "the whole cases" is wrong.
This approach ___ not be suitable for ve: This approach ___ not be suitable for very small companies. (choose the hedge)
might not be suitable (có thể không phù: "Might not be suitable" is a gentle hedge. "Will not" and "must not" state a fact or a ban; "can never" is too absolute.
Students from wealthier families ___ to: Students from wealthier families ___ to perform better in exams. (a general trend)
tend to + verb: for general trends.
Demand for electric cars is ___ to rise: Demand for electric cars is ___ to rise over the next decade. (a strong possibility)
be likely to + verb: highly probable.
tend to + verb makes the claim less absolute.
Bị động khách quan: It is widely believe: Impersonal passive: It is widely believed that + clause.
It appears that + mệnh đề: kết luận dè d: It appears that + clause: a cautious conclusion – drop clearly.
tend to + V: không khẳng định cho mọi tr: tend to + verb: you don't claim it's true in every case.
be likely to + V thay cho will tuyệt đối: be likely to + verb instead of an absolute will.
appear là nội động từ: It appears that…,: Appear is intransitive: It appears that…, never in the passive.
Rào đón bằng động từ khuyết thiếu may +: Hedge with the modal may + base verb to make the claim less certain.
appear + to be + tính từ (dường như…) là: appear + to be + adjective (= seems…) is a formal hedge.
The data ___ to suggest that older drive: The data ___ to suggest that older drivers are safer. (a tendency)
tend/seem/appear + to V để làm nhẹ mức k: tend/seem/appear + to + verb softens a claim; in academic writing, data can be treated as singular (tends) or plural (tend).
It is ___ that the new policy will reduc: It is ___ that the new policy will reduce traffic. (a possibility)
It is likely/possible that… (có khả năng: It is likely/possible that… is a common hedge in academic writing.
\"may\" cho thấy kết luận còn dè dặt; \": "May" shows the conclusion is tentative; "proves" expresses certainty and contradicts it → suggests.
These findings ___ indicate that sleep q: These findings ___ indicate that sleep quality affects exam performance. (possibly – a tentative claim)
Động từ khuyết thiếu may/might/could + V: The modals may/might/could + base verb lower the level of certainty. "Must" is wrong because it makes the claim strong again.
There is ___ evidence that bilingual chi: There is ___ evidence that bilingual children are better at switching tasks. (some – not absolute)
some evidence (một số bằng chứng) dè dặt: "Some evidence" is more cautious than "clear/strong evidence". "A" is wrong because evidence is uncountable.
be likely to + V (có khả năng) – tính từ: be likely to + verb (= probably will) – likely is an adjective. "Like" is wrong because there's no structure "be like to + verb".
Trạng từ arguably (có thể cho rằng) đứng: The adverb arguably goes before a superlative to hedge. "Arguable" is an adjective and can't modify the whole phrase.
There is some evidence that + mệnh đề: t: There is some evidence that + clause: present the conclusion as a limited finding, not an absolute fact.
may + be + V3 (bị động dè dặt). Không vi: may + be + past participle (a cautious passive). Don't write "may is caused" – after may you need the base form be.
It could be argued that… thay cho \"Ever: "It could be argued that…" instead of "Everyone agrees" – avoids overgeneralising, a common reason to lose Task Response marks.
can + V nói về khả năng chứ không phải l: can + verb talks about possibility, not "always"; adding "some" avoids generalising about all children.
seem + to V; và \"prove\" quá chắc chắn,: seem + to + verb; "prove" is too certain and contradicts "seem". Use: seem to suggest.
Cấu trúc It is + tính từ + that…: possib: The structure It is + adjective + that…: possible. "Possibly" is an adverb and can't follow be as the complement.
Câu hỏi đuôi: khẳng định → đuôi phủ định: Question tags: positive sentence → negative tag (isn't it?), negative sentence → positive tag (is it?).
